supporting_observations.claim: WS-BCARTER-01 made repeated connections to the internal proxy at approximately five-minute intervals during the alert window; examples include 13:36:22, 13:41:10, 13:46:34, 13:51:47, 13:55:57, 14:01:14, and 14:06:22 UTC.
The cited periodic-session records identify the destination only as the internal proxy at 10.30.20.30:8080; they do not identify the external HTTPS hostname or the originating process.
The connection cadence is consistent with the approximately five-minute update-check interval documented for ChartMate, but these records do not establish that ChartMate generated the connections.

At about 14:10 UTC, OneDrive started and Chrome made successful SharePoint requests; these records show Microsoft-related activity near the end of the alert window, but do not tie it to the earlier periodic sessions.

known_telemetry_limitations: The listed records for the periodic connections are Zeek summaries to the internal proxy and do not include the external hostname or process attribution.
The available proxy records show identifiable destinations for other activity, such as SharePoint and Teams, but do not provide destination details for the cited periodic sessions.
claims_not_established: Whether the periodic connections reached an approved service such as ChartMate or an unapproved destination.
Which process or application initiated the periodic connections.
Whether the repeated traffic carried malicious instructions, data, or other payloads.
Whether the periodic connections were caused by the scheduled svc-claimsync password rotation; the supplied periodic-session records do not identify that service account or job.
additional_evidence_needed: Proxy logs covering each periodic connection, including CONNECT or request hostname, outcome, and any available TLS or URL details.
Endpoint network telemetry that attributes each connection to a process, executable path, user, and process ancestry.
Process and software inventory for WS-BCARTER-01, including verification of whether ChartMate is installed and whether its updater ran during the interval.
Relevant endpoint and proxy telemetry before and after the review window to determine whether the cadence and destination persist.
